subject: Replacing a covariance matrix in lavaan.mi object

messages.author: 62939dad0d7082c7
messages.subject: Replacing a covariance matrix in lavaan.mi object
parts:
Hello,

I am wondering whether it is possible to extract a covariance matrix from a lavaan.mi object, perform an operation on the covariance matrix, and then in the lavaan.mi object, "replace" the original covariance matrix with the matrix that has had some operation performed on it?

So, something like:

# extract a covariance matrix from lavaan.mi object named 'Fit.Null.Model.20'
x1 <- Fit.Null.Model.20@SampleStatsList[[1]][["cov"]]

# do some kind of operation on x1

# then replace SampleStatsList[[1]][["cov"]] with x1
?????

Does anyone know if (a) replacing a covariance matrix in a lavaan.mi object is possble and (b) what the syntax would be to do so?

Many thanks in advance,

Ian.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Replacing a covariance matrix in lavaan.mi object
parts:
Ian,
The below script confirms that It is possible.  However, as you can see, it creates an inconsistent object because other elements have already been computed reflecting the original covariance matrix. Also, as you are probably aware, there is no guarantee that the internal structure of such objects remains the same across updates.

## impose missing data for example
HSMiss <- HolzingerSwineford1939[ , c(paste("x", 1:9, sep = ""),
                                      "ageyr","agemo","school")]
set.seed(12345)
HSMiss$x5 <- ifelse(HSMiss$x5 <= quantile(HSMiss$x5, .3), NA, HSMiss$x5)
age <- HSMiss$ageyr + HSMiss$agemo/12
HSMiss$x9 <- ifelse(age <= quantile(age, .3), NA, HSMiss$x9)

## specify CFA model from lavaan's ?cfa help page
HS.model <- '
  visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
  speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'

## impute data within runMI...
out1 <- cfa.mi(HS.model, data = HSMiss, m = 20, seed = 12345,
               miArgs = list(noms = "school"))
summary(out1)



x1 <- out1@SampleStatsList[[1]][["cov"]]
x1
x2 <- x1 * 10
x2

out1@SampleStatsList[[1]][["cov"]] <- x2
out1@SampleStatsList[[1]][["cov"]]

summary(out1)

Keith
